title: Directional derivative of a Lipschitz map along DΦ(w)s equals D(f∘Φ)(w)s (Simon Ch. 2, 4.7/4.10)
statement: Let n, P, Q ∈ ℕ, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and w ∈ ℝⁿ. Suppose f is K-Lipschitz (K ≥ 0) on some neighbourhood V of Φ(w), Φ is differentiable at w, and f∘Φ is differentiable at w. Then for every s ∈ ℝⁿ the map t ↦ f(Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s) (t ∈ ℝ) has derivative D(f∘Φ)(w)s at t = 0, where DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w and D(f∘Φ)(w) = fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w.
lean_statement: ∀ (n P Q : ℕ) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (w : Eucl n), (∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 (Φ w), LipschitzOnWith K f V) → DifferentiableAt ℝ Φ w → DifferentiableAt ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w → ∀ s : Eucl n, HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => f (Φ w + t • fderiv ℝ Φ w s)) (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w s) 0
